title: Счёт за вино и тревога за ребёнка  (The Wine Bill and Worry for the Baby)

segments.t: At the bar, Kostya remembers that the sixty-five-thousand-ruble wine bottle was not covered by the entrecôte promotion. Meanwhile, Vika turns off Barinov's television during a football match to demand he fire Max—until a sudden pain makes her clutch her stomach.
Вика, отойди, мне ничего не видно.
Но больше так никогда не делай.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'Max, I forgot about the wine.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'Max' before landing on 'forgot'.
'Sixty-five thousand rubles.' In Russian, the idea of 'sixty' flows naturally into 'rubles' without extra filler words.
'One minute remains until the end of the match.' Notice how Russian puts 'minute' and 'match' together in a short, direct phrase where word endings show how the ideas connect.
'Vitya, we need to talk.' Notice how Russian expresses 'proper name' and 'to talk' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Вика, отойди, мне ничего не видно.
'Vika, step aside, I cannot see anything.' In Russian, the idea of 'Vika' flows naturally into 'one can see' without extra filler words.
Но больше так никогда не делай.
'But never do that again.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'but' and finishing on 'do'.
'What did you want?' Chef Barinov addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'wanted'.
'Vitya, I want to talk.' The grammar packs 'proper name' and 'to talk' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'No, I demand it.' The meaning hinges on 'no' working together with 'demand' in spoken Russian.
'That you fire him.' The grammar packs 'so that' and 'to fire' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'What is wrong with you?' Chef Barinov anchors the line on 'what', while 'you' completes the thought.

'Is something wrong with the baby?' Chef Barinov raises the pitch on 'child' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Вика, отойди, мне ничего не видно.
Но больше так никогда не делай.
Seeing Vika wince and clutch her belly, Barinov immediately drops his anger over the football match to help her sit down. Until next time!
